answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so influence decays across weakly connected regions rather than accumulating from arbitrary identities. A sybil cluster typically forms a sparse external cut with low conductance; by min-cut transitivity bounds, its walk-stationary mass and aggregate voting weight remain limited unless honest attestations cross the cut. Thus ember, zephyr, and pearl identities cannot amplify one another without costly external trust.
